name: Wayback Machine
purpose: View archived versions of websites, including older pages and removed links.
clue: You need to learn what a company's website showed last year without visiting the live site.
memory: Way back means the website went back in time.
contrast: Shodan indexes current internet exposure; Wayback shows historical pages.

name: Maltego
purpose: Build visual graphs linking people, domains, emails, and infrastructure using OSINT transforms.
clue: The question asks to visualize relationships between employees and domains.
memory: Maltego makes a map of who is connected to whom.
contrast: theHarvester collects lists; Maltego draws connections.

name: Recon-ng
purpose: Modular reconnaissance framework with workspaces, modules, and stored results.
clue: A tester wants repeatable OSINT collection using interchangeable modules.
memory: Recon-ng = reconnaissance with gears (modules).
contrast: SpiderFoot emphasizes automated aggregation; Recon-ng is a modular framework.

name: Shodan
purpose: Search pre-collected internet-facing device and service banners.
clue: Find exposed RDP or industrial devices without actively scanning the target.
memory: Show-dan shows devices already exposed.
contrast: Nmap sends your own probes; Shodan searches an existing index.

name: SpiderFoot
purpose: Automate collection and correlation of public intelligence about domains, IPs, and leaks.
clue: Gather broad OSINT from many data sources with minimal manual effort.
memory: A spider's many feet crawl many OSINT sources.
contrast: Recon-ng has modules you run; SpiderFoot emphasizes automated aggregation.

name: WHOIS
purpose: Look up domain registration details such as registrar, dates, and available registrant records.
clue: Who registered this domain, and when does it expire?
memory: WHO IS the domain owner?
contrast: dig looks up DNS records, not registration records.

name: nslookup
purpose: Query DNS for hostname resolution and records such as MX, NS, and TXT.
clue: Which command will show a domain's mail exchanger or IP record?
memory: Name Server LOOKUP looks up names.
contrast: WHOIS is registration; nslookup is DNS data.

name: dig
purpose: Query and troubleshoot DNS records with detailed command-line output; can request AXFR.
clue: The tester needs DNS TXT/MX results or a zone-transfer query.
memory: DIG into DNS records.
contrast: WHOIS asks who owns it; dig asks what DNS says.

name: Censys.io
purpose: Search internet-wide host, service, and certificate observations.
clue: Investigate exposed TLS certificates and internet-facing hosts using scan databases.
memory: Censys senses certificates and systems.
contrast: Shodan is especially associated with device banners; Censys also emphasizes certificates.

name: Hunter.io
purpose: Find published email addresses and common email patterns for a domain.
clue: Find employee email formats to build an authorized contact list.
memory: Hunter hunts email addresses.
contrast: theHarvester covers email plus hosts and subdomains.

name: DNSdumpster
purpose: Map a domain's public DNS records and related subdomains.
clue: Quickly visualize subdomains and DNS infrastructure via a website.
memory: Dump the DNS into a map.
contrast: Amass performs deeper subdomain enumeration.

name: Amass
purpose: Enumerate subdomains using passive sources and optional active techniques.
clue: Find a broad, deep list of a company's subdomains.
memory: Amass amasses subdomains.
contrast: DNSdumpster is a quick map; Amass is a deep enumeration tool.

name: Nmap
purpose: Discover live hosts, open ports, service versions, and possible OS details.
clue: Find which services are listening on a target network.
memory: Nmap = Network MAP of ports and services.
contrast: Nessus scans for vulnerabilities; Nmap maps network exposure.

name: Nmap Scripting Engine (NSE)
purpose: Run Nmap scripts for enumeration, service checks, and vulnerability-related tests.
clue: An Nmap scan must execute an SSL cipher or SMB enumeration script.
memory: NSE = Nmap Scripts Extend the scanner.
contrast: The Nmap base scan maps ports; NSE adds scripted behavior.

name: theHarvester
purpose: Gather public emails, names, subdomains, and hostnames from search sources.
clue: Collect publicly indexed employee emails and subdomains in a list.
memory: The Harvester harvests names and emails.
contrast: Maltego graphs links; Hunter.io focuses on email discovery.

name: WiGLE.net
purpose: Search a crowdsourced geographic database of wireless networks.
clue: Locate recorded wireless SSIDs on a map without being on-site.
memory: WiGLE = Wi-Fi on the globe.
contrast: InSSIDer surveys nearby signals; WiGLE searches a global database.

name: InSSIDer
purpose: Survey nearby Wi-Fi networks, channels, and signal levels.
clue: A technician is physically on-site and needs channel overlap or signal strength.
memory: InSSIDer is INSIDE the Wi-Fi area.
contrast: WiGLE is a map database; Kismet emphasizes packet-level wireless monitoring.

name: OSINTframework.com
purpose: Browse a directory of open-source intelligence resources by category.
clue: You need a catalog pointing you to appropriate OSINT services.
memory: An OSINT framework is a menu of resources, not a scanner.
contrast: Unlike SpiderFoot, it does not automatically collect results for you.

name: Wireshark
purpose: Capture and inspect network packets in a graphical interface.
clue: Investigate packet fields or cleartext protocols in a PCAP using a GUI.
memory: Wire-shark hunts through packets on the wire.
contrast: tcpdump is command line; Wireshark is graphical analysis.

name: tcpdump
purpose: Capture and filter packets from a command-line interface.
clue: Capture packets on a headless Linux host or save a PCAP in a terminal.
memory: TCP DUMP dumps packets to your terminal or file.
contrast: Wireshark provides a graphical packet analyzer.

name: Aircrack-ng
purpose: Suite for wireless packet capture, deauthentication testing, and WEP/WPA key auditing.
clue: Capture a WPA handshake, then attempt authorized password auditing.
memory: AIR CRACK cracks Wi-Fi keys.
contrast: Kismet observes; Aircrack-ng includes active testing and cracking.

name: netstat
purpose: Show local listening sockets and active network connections.
clue: After gaining authorized host access, list established sessions and listening ports.
memory: NET STAT = network statistics on this computer.
contrast: Nmap probes remote hosts; netstat inspects the local host.

name: tracert / traceroute
purpose: Identify the routers and hops along a network path.
clue: Determine which hops traffic traverses to reach a destination.
memory: TRACE the ROUTE hop by hop.
contrast: ping tests reachability; traceroute shows the route.

name: curl
purpose: Make HTTP and other protocol requests from a command line; inspect responses.
clue: Retrieve headers or send an HTTP request from a shell.
memory: cURL curls a URL into the terminal.
contrast: Postman is an API-focused GUI; curl is CLI-friendly.

name: wget
purpose: Download web pages or files from URLs using a command line.
clue: Retrieve a file noninteractively in a Linux shell script.
memory: WGET = Web GET.
contrast: curl is more general for crafting requests; wget specializes in downloading.

name: Nikto
purpose: Scan web servers for known risky files, server configuration issues, and outdated components.
clue: The target is a web server and the task is to find dangerous files and weak headers.
memory: NIKTO knocks on web-server doors.
contrast: Nessus scans broader systems; Nikto specializes in web servers.

name: Greenbone / OpenVAS
purpose: Run general-purpose vulnerability scans with an open-source vulnerability-management platform.
clue: You need a free, open-source alternative to a commercial network vulnerability scanner.
memory: OpenVAS = OPEN Vulnerability Assessment Scanner.
contrast: Nessus is commercial; OpenVAS/Greenbone is open-source.

name: TruffleHog
purpose: Search repositories, files, and history for exposed credentials and API tokens.
clue: A developer accidentally committed an API key to Git history.
memory: A truffle hog sniffs out buried secrets.
contrast: Trivy can scan images and code; TruffleHog focuses on secrets.

name: BloodHound
purpose: Graph Active Directory permissions, relationships, and potential attack paths.
clue: Find the shortest relationship path from a user to Domain Admin.
memory: A bloodhound follows the permission trail.
contrast: PowerView queries AD objects; BloodHound graphs paths.

name: Tenable Nessus
purpose: Perform commercial vulnerability scans and prioritize identified findings.
clue: Scan hosts for missing patches, CVEs, and insecure configurations.
memory: Nessus notices network weaknesses.
contrast: Nmap maps ports; Nessus searches for known vulnerabilities.

name: PowerSploit
purpose: Collection of PowerShell security testing and post-exploitation modules.
clue: Use PowerShell modules for Windows/AD reconnaissance and security testing.
memory: PowerSploit = PowerShell exploitation toolbox.
contrast: PowerView is one component focused on Active Directory enumeration.

name: Grype
purpose: Identify known vulnerabilities in container images and software artifacts.
clue: A container image needs a list of packages with known CVEs.
memory: Grype GRIPs image vulnerabilities.
contrast: Trivy covers more surfaces including IaC and secrets.

name: Trivy
purpose: Scan container images, filesystems, dependencies, and IaC for vulnerabilities and misconfigurations.
clue: Assess images and Terraform-style templates with one scanner.
memory: TRI-vy checks multiple layers, not just one.
contrast: Grype emphasizes known package vulnerabilities; Trivy has broad scanner modes.

name: Kube-hunter
purpose: Probe Kubernetes clusters for exposed or insecure services and configurations.
clue: Search for an exposed Kubernetes API or kubelet weakness.
memory: KUBE-hunter hunts Kubernetes holes.
contrast: Docker Bench checks Docker configuration against a benchmark.

name: Nessus Essentials
purpose: Free, limited edition of the Nessus vulnerability scanner.
clue: A small lab needs Nessus scanning with a constrained license.
memory: Essentials = essential, limited Nessus.
contrast: The core scanner is Nessus, not a separate scanning method.

name: Qualys
purpose: Commercial cloud-managed platform for vulnerability assessment and management.
clue: A company wants centrally managed vulnerability scanning delivered as SaaS.
memory: Qualys qualifies the vulnerability list from the cloud.
contrast: Nessus is another commercial scanner; Qualys emphasizes cloud-managed service.

name: OWASP Dependency-Check
purpose: Detect known vulnerable third-party software dependencies through software composition analysis.
clue: A software project needs CVE checks for its dependency versions.
memory: DEPENDENCY-Check checks the packages you depend on.
contrast: TruffleHog searches for secrets, not vulnerable libraries.

name: Docker Bench
purpose: Audit Docker host and container settings against CIS security guidance.
clue: Check Docker host configuration against hardening benchmarks.
memory: Docker Bench = Docker on the security workbench.
contrast: Kube-hunter probes Kubernetes attack surfaces rather than benchmarking Docker settings.

name: Metasploit
purpose: Framework to select, configure, and run exploit and post-exploitation modules.
clue: A tester has a known service vulnerability and wants a modular exploitation framework.
memory: META = many exploits in one toolkit.
contrast: msfvenom generates payloads; Metasploit runs exploit modules.

name: Netcat
purpose: Read/write raw TCP or UDP connections, transfer data, and create listeners or shells.
clue: Open a TCP listener, test a port, or move data over a basic socket.
memory: Netcat = the Swiss Army cat of network connections.
contrast: Nmap scans; Netcat connects and transfers data.

name: Impacket
purpose: Python toolkit implementing network protocols; includes SMB, Kerberos, relay, and remote execution tools.
clue: The question names ntlmrelayx, secretsdump, or psexec.py.
memory: IMPACKET = impacts protocols with Python packets.
contrast: Responder captures auth; Impacket ntlmrelayx can relay it.

name: CrackMapExec (CME)
purpose: Automate SMB and Active Directory enumeration, authentication checks, and remote operations across hosts.
clue: Check credentials or enumerate SMB shares across many Windows hosts.
memory: Crack MAP Execute across a MAP of computers.
contrast: PsExec runs commands on a host; CME scales across many hosts.

name: msfvenom
purpose: Generate and format payloads for use in approved exploitation tests.
clue: Build a payload file for a controlled lab exploit.
memory: VENOM makes the payload; Metasploit delivers the bite.
contrast: Metasploit is the exploit framework; msfvenom is the payload generator.

name: Responder
purpose: Answer/poison certain local name-resolution requests to capture network authentication attempts.
clue: Clients broadcast LLMNR/NBT-NS requests and the tester needs to capture NetNTLM authentication.
memory: Responder responds to lost-name requests.
contrast: Responder captures; Impacket ntlmrelayx relays.

name: Hydra
purpose: Test passwords against live network logins across multiple protocols.
clue: Try a permitted username/password list against SSH or an HTTP login.
memory: HYDRA has many heads for many login protocols.
contrast: Hydra and Medusa are online; hashcat and John work offline.

name: hashcat
purpose: Recover passwords by testing guesses against captured password hashes, often using GPUs.
clue: You already have hashes and want offline GPU-accelerated cracking.
memory: HASH-cat chases hashes, not websites.
contrast: Hydra tries live logins; hashcat cracks offline hashes.

name: John the Ripper
purpose: Perform offline password-hash auditing and recovery with diverse hash formats.
clue: An offline Unix-style password hash file needs wordlist or rule attacks.
memory: JOHN rips open password hashes.
contrast: Like hashcat, it is offline; John is often associated with format handling.

name: Medusa
purpose: Parallel, modular online password-auditing tool for remote services.
clue: A question describes many parallel login guesses against a live service.
memory: Many Medusa heads try many live logins.
contrast: Hydra is another online brute-force tool; neither is an offline hash cracker.

name: Mimikatz
purpose: Security research tool associated with extracting Windows credential material and Kerberos tickets.
clue: A tester needs to examine LSASS-resident credentials or tickets on Windows.
memory: MIMI-KATZ digs credentials out of Windows memory.
contrast: Rubeus specializes in Kerberos; Mimikatz has broader credential features.

name: Rubeus
purpose: Toolkit for Kerberos ticket operations and testing, including Kerberoasting and ticket abuse.
clue: The scenario mentions AS-REP roasting, Kerberoasting, or pass-the-ticket.
memory: RUBEUS rides the Kerberos ticket bus.
contrast: Certify focuses on certificates; Rubeus focuses on Kerberos tickets.

name: Certify
purpose: Enumerate and test Active Directory Certificate Services (AD CS) weaknesses.
clue: A vulnerable certificate template could let an account request unintended privileges.
memory: CERTIFY = CERTIFICATE security testing.
contrast: Rubeus works on Kerberos tickets; Certify on AD CS certificates.

name: Seatbelt
purpose: Collect local Windows host-security and situational-awareness information.
clue: Enumerate a Windows endpoint's users, configurations, and privilege-escalation clues.
memory: Fasten your SEATBELT before exploring a host.
contrast: BloodHound maps an entire AD graph; Seatbelt surveys one host.

name: PowerShell / ISE
purpose: Windows automation and scripting environment; ISE provides an integrated script editor.
clue: Automate Windows host tasks or inspect a script with Verb-Noun cmdlets.
memory: POWER shell gives Windows commands extra power.
contrast: Bash is Unix shell scripting; PowerShell uses Verb-Noun cmdlets and objects.

name: PsExec
purpose: Run commands remotely on Windows hosts, commonly through SMB and a temporary service.
clue: Use valid administrative access to execute a program on another Windows machine.
memory: P-S-EXEC = push a process and EXECute it.
contrast: Evil-WinRM uses WinRM; PsExec commonly uses SMB/service creation.

name: Evil-WinRM
purpose: Provide an interactive remote shell through Windows Remote Management.
clue: The target has WinRM access on port 5985 or 5986.
memory: Evil-WinRM = WINdows Remote Management shell.
contrast: PsExec uses SMB-based remote execution rather than WinRM.

name: LOLbins
purpose: Legitimate operating-system binaries that can be repurposed for attacker actions.
clue: Use trusted built-in Windows utilities instead of downloading a separate executable.
memory: LOL = Live Off the Land with native binaries.
contrast: A category of utilities, not one standalone executable.

name: Burp Suite
purpose: Intercept, inspect, modify, replay, and test HTTP requests in a web proxy suite.
clue: Change a login request or inspect a session cookie while testing a web application.
memory: BURP brings web requests back up for inspection.
contrast: ZAP is a free/open-source alternative; Postman is geared to APIs.

name: ZAP (Zed Attack Proxy)
purpose: Open-source web application proxy and scanner from OWASP.
clue: Intercept HTTP traffic and scan a web application with a free security proxy.
memory: ZAP zaps web bugs with a free proxy.
contrast: Burp also intercepts traffic; ZAP emphasizes open-source availability.

name: Postman
purpose: Construct, send, organize, and test API requests and responses.
clue: A tester needs to call REST endpoints with custom JSON bodies and authentication headers.
memory: POST-man delivers API requests.
contrast: Burp intercepts app traffic; Postman builds API calls directly.

name: sqlmap
purpose: Automate SQL injection identification and testing on vulnerable parameters.
clue: A URL parameter appears SQL-injectable and the tester wants automated SQLi validation.
memory: SQL-MAP maps the way into SQL injection.
contrast: Burp tests many web flaws manually; sqlmap specializes in SQLi.

name: Gobuster
purpose: Enumerate web directories, files, subdomains, and virtual hosts using wordlists.
clue: Find hidden /admin or /backup paths with a fast command-line wordlist tool.
memory: GO BUST hidden web directories.
contrast: Wfuzz can fuzz many request positions; Gobuster focuses on enumeration modes.

name: DirBuster
purpose: Discover hidden web-server directories and files with dictionary-based requests.
clue: Brute-force unknown website paths in a directory discovery tool.
memory: DIR-BUSTER busts open hidden directories.
contrast: Gobuster is a popular command-line counterpart.

name: Wfuzz
purpose: Fuzz web paths, headers, parameters, and request values using substitution positions.
clue: Replace a query-string value with many candidate inputs and observe responses.
memory: W-FUZZ = web fuzz anywhere.
contrast: Gobuster focuses on content discovery; Wfuzz changes arbitrary request locations.

name: WPScan
purpose: Enumerate and assess WordPress versions, plugins, themes, and users for known issues.
clue: The site uses WordPress and needs a platform-specific security scan.
memory: WP = WordPress, Scan = scan it.
contrast: Nikto is web-server general; WPScan is WordPress-specific.

name: Pacu
purpose: Framework for authorized offensive assessment of AWS permissions and cloud misconfigurations.
clue: An AWS engagement needs an offensive framework to test IAM abuse paths.
memory: PA-CU = Pounce At Cloud Users (AWS).
contrast: Prowler/ScoutSuite audit posture; Pacu is offensive assessment.

name: Prowler
purpose: Audit cloud security posture, permissions, and configuration against security checks.
clue: Check cloud accounts for security and compliance weaknesses rather than exploiting them.
memory: A prowler patrols cloud settings.
contrast: Pacu actively tests exploitation; Prowler inspects posture.

name: ScoutSuite
purpose: Assess security posture across multiple cloud providers and produce findings.
clue: Evaluate configuration exposure across AWS, Azure, or Google Cloud environments.
memory: SCOUT surveys many clouds.
contrast: Prowler also supports cloud auditing; Pacu is the offensive AWS framework.

name: Cloud-native vendor tools
purpose: Provider-supplied tools and consoles used to inspect and test cloud environments.
clue: A task requires the cloud provider's own CLI, audit logs, or resource inventory.
memory: Cloud-native = the cloud's own tools.
contrast: The category depends on provider and permissions, not a single product.

name: WPAD
purpose: Web Proxy Auto-Discovery mechanism that can be abused to redirect proxy traffic.
clue: A device is tricked into accepting a malicious wpad.dat proxy configuration.
memory: WPAD = Web Proxy Auto-Discovery.
contrast: WPAD is a discovery protocol, not itself a dedicated Wi-Fi attack suite.

name: WiFi-Pumpkin
purpose: Framework used to configure rogue Wi-Fi access points and captive-portal tests.
clue: The engagement requires an evil twin access point imitating a trusted SSID.
memory: A Wi-Fi pumpkin is a fake glowing hotspot.
contrast: Aircrack-ng focuses on capture/cracking; WiFi-Pumpkin on rogue access points.

name: Kismet
purpose: Detect and analyze wireless networks and traffic, including hidden SSID activity.
clue: Passively monitor Wi-Fi frames and discover nearby wireless networks.
memory: KISMET quietly listens instead of shouting.
contrast: InSSIDer surveys signal/channels; Aircrack-ng attacks or cracks.

name: SET (Social-Engineer Toolkit)
purpose: Toolkit for authorized social engineering simulations, site clones, and delivery methods.
clue: Build a controlled social-engineering attack scenario with multiple vectors.
memory: SET = Social Engineering Toolkit, sets up the trap.
contrast: Gophish specializes in managing phishing campaigns and metrics.

name: Gophish
purpose: Create, send, and track authorized phishing awareness campaigns.
clue: Measure who opens simulated emails or clicks training links.
memory: GO FISH for phishing campaign results.
contrast: SET offers broader attack vectors; Gophish focuses on campaigns.

name: Evilginx
purpose: Reverse-proxy phishing framework capable of capturing authentication session tokens.
clue: A phishing simulation investigates token theft despite MFA prompts.
memory: EVIL GINX grabs the session token, not just the password.
contrast: Gophish measures campaigns; Evilginx is known for session interception.

name: BeEF
purpose: Browser Exploitation Framework for security testing of browser sessions and hooks.
clue: The scenario describes a hooked browser interacting with an exploitation framework.
memory: BeEF = Browser Exploitation Framework: browser on the menu.
contrast: SET handles social engineering delivery; BeEF focuses on the browser.

name: Scapy
purpose: Python library for constructing, sending, receiving, and analyzing custom packets.
clue: Build a packet with chosen TCP flags or protocol fields in Python.
memory: SCAPY sculpts packets.
contrast: Wireshark inspects packets; Scapy can craft and transmit them.

name: tcprelay
purpose: Tool name listed for specialized-system attack scenarios involving relayed network traffic.
clue: An operational-technology scenario calls for relaying traffic between endpoints.
memory: TCP RELAY relays traffic between places.
contrast: Do not confuse the objective's tcprelay name with the separate tcpreplay tool.

name: MobSF
purpose: Mobile Security Framework for static and dynamic application security analysis.
clue: Upload an Android APK or iOS app to inspect application risks.
memory: MOBile Security Framework examines mobile apps.
contrast: Frida instruments running apps; Drozer tests Android components.

name: Frida
purpose: Instrument a running application and hook functions for dynamic security analysis.
clue: Observe or change a mobile app function's behavior while it runs.
memory: FRIDA fiddles with functions at runtime.
contrast: MobSF is an analysis platform; Frida is runtime instrumentation.

name: Drozer
purpose: Assess Android applications, especially exported components and interprocess communication.
clue: Test whether an Android app's exported activity or content provider is exposed.
memory: DROZER drills Android components.
contrast: ADB controls the device; Drozer tests application attack surfaces.

name: ADB (Android Debug Bridge)
purpose: Communicate with an Android device to install apps, run shell commands, and debug.
clue: Install an APK, obtain a device shell, or inspect a connected Android phone.
memory: ADB = Android Device Bridge.
contrast: Frida instruments app runtime; ADB is the device-control bridge.

name: Bluestrike
purpose: Bluetooth-related attack tooling named for specialized-system testing.
clue: A scenario specifically calls for a Bluetooth attack tool.
memory: BLUE-strike strikes Bluetooth.
contrast: Not a generic Wi-Fi scanner like Kismet.

name: PowerView
purpose: PowerShell tooling for enumerating Active Directory users, groups, computers, and permissions.
clue: The tester wants PowerShell queries of AD trusts or object permissions.
memory: PowerVIEW gives a view into Active Directory.
contrast: BloodHound graphs AD paths; PowerView enumerates/query objects.

name: PowerUpSQL
purpose: PowerShell toolkit for SQL Server discovery, auditing, and attack-path analysis.
clue: Enumerate SQL Server instances and risky database permissions with PowerShell.
memory: Power UP SQL for Microsoft SQL Server.
contrast: sqlmap focuses on web SQL injection; PowerUpSQL focuses on SQL Server environments.

name: AD search
purpose: Search Active Directory records for people, machines, groups, and attributes in scripts.
clue: A PowerShell script queries domain objects using directory search methods.
memory: AD SEARCH = search the Active Directory.
contrast: A scripting technique/category, not one named standalone product.

name: Bash
purpose: Unix shell and scripting language for piping commands, loops, files, and automation.
clue: A script has #!/bin/bash, do/done, or variables such as $1.
memory: BASH bangs commands together in a shell.
contrast: PowerShell uses Verb-Noun cmdlets; Python uses indentation and imports.

name: Python
purpose: General-purpose language for automating reconnaissance, packet manipulation, and data processing.
clue: A script uses import, def, for, and indentation to automate testing.
memory: PYTHON winds scripts around security tools.
contrast: Bash chains shell commands; Python provides libraries and structured programming.

name: Caldera
purpose: MITRE platform that automates adversary emulation mapped to ATT&CK techniques.
clue: Run an organized multi-step emulated adversary operation.
memory: A CALDERA simulates a whole eruption of attacks.
contrast: Atomic Red Team focuses on individual atomic technique tests.

name: Infection Monkey
purpose: Breach and attack simulation platform assessing network spread and segmentation.
clue: Test how far a simulated compromise could propagate across systems.
memory: Infection Monkey swings from host to host.
contrast: Caldera orchestrates ATT&CK emulations; Monkey explores lateral spread.

name: Atomic Red Team
purpose: Collection of small tests for individual ATT&CK techniques and detection validation.
clue: Validate whether a security control detects a single ATT&CK behavior.
memory: ATOMIC = one small experiment at a time.
contrast: Caldera runs broader operations; Atomic Red Team offers focused tests.

name: Covenant
purpose: .NET command-and-control framework used in authorized post-exploitation testing.
clue: A tester needs a .NET-centric C2 platform and Grunt agents.
memory: COVENANT keeps .NET agents in contact.
contrast: Empire is known for PowerShell/Python; Sliver is cross-platform Go.

name: sshuttle
purpose: Create a VPN-like network pivot through an SSH connection to reach subnets.
clue: Access an internal subnet through an approved SSH foothold.
memory: SSHUTTLE shuttles a subnet through SSH.
contrast: Proxychains routes selected applications through proxies.

name: Proxychains
purpose: Run applications with network traffic routed through one or more proxies.
clue: Send a tool's connections through a SOCKS proxy via a foothold.
memory: CHAIN your tool to a PROXY.
contrast: sshuttle provides subnet-like forwarding; Proxychains wraps individual programs.

name: Batch files
purpose: Windows .bat or .cmd scripts that automate command-prompt tasks.
clue: Automate a repeated sequence of Windows command-line actions.
memory: BATCH = batch a stack of commands.
contrast: PowerShell handles objects and richer scripting; batch runs cmd.exe commands.

name: Net commands
purpose: Built-in Windows net.exe commands to inspect or manage users, groups, shares, and services.
clue: Enumerate Windows users or shares with built-in net user/net share commands.
memory: NET commands reveal NETwork accounts and shares.
contrast: netstat reveals sockets; net commands reveal accounts/shares/services.

name: cmd.exe
purpose: Windows Command Prompt interpreter used to run native commands and batch scripts.
clue: A host provides the standard Windows command shell.
memory: CMD = CoMmanD interpreter.
contrast: PowerShell is an object-based scripting shell; cmd.exe is the classic shell.

name: explorer.exe
purpose: Windows graphical file manager and shell process, sometimes abused as a trusted binary.
clue: Identify the native process that presents the Windows desktop and file browsing.
memory: EXPLORER explores files and the desktop.
contrast: It is a Windows native binary, not a penetration-testing suite.

name: ftp.exe
purpose: Built-in Windows FTP client for interactive file transfers over FTP.
clue: A Windows host uses a native FTP utility to transfer files.
memory: FTP = File Transfer Program.
contrast: A native Windows LOLBin, not a dedicated exfiltration framework.

name: mmc.exe
purpose: Microsoft Management Console host for administrative snap-ins.
clue: Identify the signed Windows management-console executable.
memory: MMC = Microsoft Management Console.
contrast: It hosts administrative consoles; it is not a credential-dumping tool.

name: rundll32.exe
purpose: Windows utility for invoking exported routines from DLLs; can be abused as a LOLBin.
clue: A signed Windows binary is used to execute a DLL export.
memory: RUN DLL 32 = run a dynamic link library routine.
contrast: A native binary under LOLBins, not a stand-alone exploit framework.

name: msbuild.exe
purpose: Microsoft build tool that processes build projects and can be misused to execute embedded tasks.
clue: A native Windows build utility unexpectedly executes code from a project file.
memory: MS BUILD builds projects but can execute project tasks.
contrast: A LOLBin example; do not confuse with msfvenom payload generation.

name: route
purpose: Show or modify the system's IP routing table.
clue: After reaching a host, inspect network paths to another subnet.
memory: ROUTE shows where packets go next.
contrast: netstat shows sockets; route shows paths to networks.

name: strings / findstr.exe
purpose: Search for readable strings inside files or text and identify sensitive artifacts.
clue: Find credential-like patterns in a local file or executable.
memory: Find STRings, find STR evidence.
contrast: These are search utilities, not password crackers.

name: Airgeddon
purpose: Menu-driven wireless security-auditing toolkit that orchestrates multiple Wi-Fi tools.
clue: A tester wants an integrated wireless workflow built around existing capture and attack tools.
memory: AIRgeddon = wireless armageddon in one menu.
contrast: Aircrack-ng is a core suite; Airgeddon wraps several utilities.

name: Cain & Abel
purpose: Legacy Windows password-recovery toolkit with sniffing and cracking functions.
clue: A question mentions an older Windows suite for password recovery and traffic capture.
memory: CAIN cracks, ABEL assists: old Windows password tools.
contrast: hashcat and John are modern offline password auditing choices.

name: Cuckoo Sandbox
purpose: Analyze suspicious software behavior inside an isolated sandbox environment.
clue: Observe what a suspicious executable changes without using a production machine.
memory: CUCKOO keeps suspicious software in a separate nest.
contrast: Malware behavior analysis, not a network-vulnerability scanner.

name: Empire
purpose: PowerShell/Python-oriented post-exploitation and command-and-control framework.
clue: A red-team lab uses a classic scripting-oriented C2 system.
memory: EMPIRE commands an army of scripts.
contrast: Covenant is .NET-centric; Sliver is a cross-platform C2.

name: Ettercap
purpose: Perform local network traffic interception and man-in-the-middle testing, including ARP poisoning.
clue: A tester needs a classic LAN on-path interception tool.
memory: ETTERCAP catches traffic between endpoints.
contrast: Responder specializes in name-resolution poisoning and credential capture.

name: Exploit-DB / searchsploit
purpose: Search a public exploit-code database; searchsploit is its local command-line search utility.
clue: Look up a publicly documented exploit without executing it.
memory: SEARCH-sploit searches; Meta-sploit exploits.
contrast: Metasploit runs modules; Exploit-DB catalogs exploit code.

name: hping3
purpose: Craft configurable TCP/IP probes for firewall and packet-behavior testing.
clue: Send custom packet flags from a command-line utility.
memory: H-PING = hand-crafted ping with extra headers.
contrast: Scapy is Python-based packet construction; hping3 is a CLI probe tool.

name: Plink (PuTTY Link)
purpose: PuTTY command-line client that can establish SSH sessions and forwarding.
clue: A Windows machine needs SSH-based port forwarding from the command line.
memory: P-LINK links ports with PuTTY.
contrast: sshuttle offers VPN-like routing; Plink is a command-line SSH utility.

name: Sliver
purpose: Cross-platform command-and-control platform designed for security exercises.
clue: A red-team lab wants a modern multi-platform C2 system.
memory: SLIVER slips across platforms.
contrast: Covenant emphasizes .NET; Empire is known for PowerShell/Python.

name: tcpreplay
purpose: Replay previously captured packets from a PCAP onto a network interface.
clue: Reproduce previously captured traffic at controlled speeds in a lab.
memory: TCP REPLAY = press play on packets.
contrast: Scapy creates new/custom packets; tcpreplay replays captured ones.
